ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, and officers against the Swiss SECO sanctions list, United Nations Security Council consolidated sanctions, EU consolidated financial sanctions, OFAC SDN list, and domestic PEP databases. For any positive PEP match or dual-citizenship with sanctioned states, Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD) is required under Art. 6 AMLA, including source-of-funds verification and senior management approval. Screening must be repeated at least every 90 days and immediately upon any newly published SECO, UN, or OFAC designation.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Swiss Central Business Index (Zefix) and Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (SOGC/SHAB) via the responsible Cantonal Commercial Register Office
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Names must be in one of the Swiss official languages (German, French, Italian, or Romansh) using Latin letters. A legal form suffix is mandatory: 'Aktiengesellschaft' or 'AG' in the German/Italian/Romansh regions, or 'Société Anonyme'/'SA' in French. For joint designations, the suffix must appear in the official language of the registered office. English transliteration is not accepted as a legal name; only Latin-script characters with numeric values in Arabic numerals or Italian/Roman numerals are permitted. Names must distinguish the company from all competing rights and must not be misleading.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Misleading name indicating a regulated activity when not licensed
Reference to public authorities or cantonal/municipal bodies without official consent
Designations of protected international organizations (e.g., Red Cross, UN)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the Cantonal Commercial Register issues a written refusal with legal basis. The applicant may file an administrative appeal with the cantonal supervisory authority within 10 days of notification, attaching the rejection decision and statutory name reservation. If the cantonal appeal is dismissed, the applicant may lodge an appeal with the Federal Administrative Court (Bundesverwaltungsgericht) within 30 days. An extension of a valid name reservation may be requested before expiration with an administrative fee, but no statutory extension is guaranteed; a fresh application is required after the 30-day window.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Restricted - A purely virtual address is not sufficient. Swiss law requires a registered office situated in the canton in which the administration is carried out. Virtual office services may be used for accepted correspondence and meeting place only if a physical location with access to corporate records, UBO register, and board minutes exists in the same municipality. For license-free digital publishing (ISIC 5820), a hybrid solution (physical serviced office + virtual business address) is generally tolerated but not a pure virtual mailbox.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 30% probability of unannounced on-site inspection within the first 24 months after incorporation, elevated to 50% if a virtual office arrangement is used without a physical board meeting location. This estimate is based on FINMA and cantonal police AML inspection patterns for medium-risk software and gaming companies.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Swiss Code of Obligations, SR 220 (Obligationenrecht / Code des obligations), Arts. 620-763 (Aktiengesellschaft); in particular Arts. 621 (formation), 629 (registered share capital), 632 (minimum capital and paid-up minimum), 634 (foundation deed), 640-646 (registered shares), 716 (Board of Directors) and 934 (application for registration); Federal Act on the Commercial Register (SR 221.411.1); Companies Names Act (SR 221.411.4); Federal Act on Games of Chance and Money Games (SR 935.0) Art. 3 scope exclusion for non-remunerated social games.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt / Registre du commerce) of the Canton of the registered office (canton to be selected by the incorporators, e.g. Zurich or Zug), supervised by the Federal Commercial Register Department (Eidgenössisches Handelsregisteramt).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Certified public Foundation Deed of Incorporation (Errichtungsakt) containing the Articles of Association (Statuten), executed before a Swiss notary, together with the electronic submission to the Commercial Register pursuant to Art. 934 OR; the registry issues a Certificate of Registration (Handelsregisterauszug / Extrait du registre du commerce).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Nominal minimum share capital of CHF 100,000 (Art. 632 para. 1 OR) of which at least 20% under each subscribed share class, and not less than CHF 50,000 in aggregate, must be paid up in cash prior to registration (Art. 632 para. 3 OR). The paid-in capital must be deposited into a blocked capital escrow account (Sperrkonto) at a FINMA-supervised bank, is reserved for use by the company in formation, and is released upon the company's registration; an undertaking to refund the deposit (Rückerstattungserklärung) is given if registration is refused or abandoned.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the incorporators adopt the Articles of Association and confirm subscription of all registered shares representing nominal capital of CHF 100,000 at par, the statutory minimum deposit being credited in full to the Company's blocked escrow account at a FINMA-supervised Swiss bank (Art. 632 OR). RESOLVED FURTHER, that the registered office of the Company be established at [registered address], [Canton], Switzerland. RESOLVED FURTHER, that [Name] be appointed Chairperson and sole member of the Board of Directors, and [Name] be appointed Managing Officer, each with individual signatory authority. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the Board be authorised to complete all Commercial Register, tax, VAT and social insurance registrations and to open banking accounts upon registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-incorporation name clearance and preparation of articles of association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register name inquiry service (Handelsregisteramt preliminary name search; online via the official SoPhIA/Zefix portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a Zefix name-availability check against protected business identifiers; define the full corporate name (e.g. '[Company] AG'), purpose clause limited to software publishing and related services, registered share capital of CHF 100,000, legal-domicile clause, board composition and audit-option statement. Engage a Swiss licensed attorney or notary to draft the statutes in accordance with Art. 629 OR. The name must not be misleading and must reflect the statutory corporate form.
required_dossiers: Proposed articles of association (draft)
Shareholders' identification documents (passport copies)
Name availability confirmation printout (Zefix search)
Authorisation letters of the founding subscribers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the selected name is refused as confusingly similar, submit three alternative distinctive names; a negative preliminary decision can be cured by adding a distinguishing element or by requesting written reasoning followed by a fresh filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of blocked capital escrow account and deposit of paid-up capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: FINMA-supervised Swiss bank (e.g. UBS Switzerland AG, Credit Suisse AG, Zuger Kantonalbank or Neobank with Swiss banking licence)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a company-in-formation escrow account (Konto mit Sperrvermerk) in the future company name. Deposit the minimum aggregate paid-up capital of CHF 50,000 (or CHF 100,000 if fully paid in before registration). The bank issues a Confirmation of Paid-up Capital (Bestätigung der Einlage) blocked for unrestricted disposition absent Commercial Register registration; source-of-funds, UBO and AML/KYC documents must be provided given the Medium_Risk_Enhanced banking profile of a social-casino games publisher.
required_dossiers: Passports plus official ID cards of all subscribers and beneficial owners
AML/KYC questionnaire and source-of-funds declaration
Draft articles of association
Letter of instruction to open an escrow account signed by all incorporators
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank queries the business purpose or AML profile, provide a supplementary narrative confirming that the games are non-remunerated social casino simulations without real-money stakes or withdrawals (Art. 3 BGS scope exclusion) and submit an internal compliance opinion; escalate to the bank's legal department for a second review cycle.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarial certification of the foundation deed and the articles of association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Swiss Public Notary (Notariat / Rechtsanwalt with notarial mandate) in the canton of the designated registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The notary reads, authenticates and formally notarises (öffentliche Beurkundung) the foundation deed containing the articles of association. Identity of all incorporators, capacity to subscribe, share subscriptions and signature specimens are verified. The notary certifies that the statutory minimum capital is deposited and blocked, and that the company's statutory organs comply with residency requirements of Board members (Swiss-resident natural person or qualified representative).
required_dossiers: Finalised foundation deed and articles of association
Bank escrow confirmation letter
Identity documents of individuals and powers of attorney of corporate subscribers
Written declarations of acceptance of office by directors and managing officer
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies deficiencies (e.g. foreign-resident board member), rectify via a board co-option declaration appointing a Swiss-resident authorised representative or adjust the by-laws clause; the notary may issue a supplementary notarial addendum before the registry filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Commercial Register registration of the stock company
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt) of the registered-office canton, electronically via the e-GR interface of the registered notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The notary submits the electronic registration application (Anmeldung) together with the sworn deed. The registry verifies the formal statutory prerequisites: name protection, expression of the share capital, deposit confirmation, capacity of signatories and the legal structure. Upon approval, the Aktiengesellschaft acquires its legal personality (Art. 643 para. 1 OR and Art. 935 OR), and the registry publishes the entry and issues the Certificate of Registration and the balance-sheet extract.
required_dossiers: Notarial certified deed of incorporation
Articles of association (official file copy)
Confirmation of paid-up capital from the escrow bank
Specimen signatures / certified signature certificates of the appointed officers
Potential audit-related declaration (actual audit waived or independent auditor appointed)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a formal query (Verfügung/Beschwerde procedure), submit the requested supplementary declarations within a 20-day statutory cure period; adverse registration decisions can be appealed to the cantonal appellate authority and further to the Swiss Federal Supreme Court.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax, VAT, and payroll withholding registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Federal Tax Administration (Eidgenössische Steuerverwaltung, ESTV) and the cantonal/communal tax authority of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company with the cantonal tax office for corporate income and capital tax assessment; communicate the commercial register data to the ESTV. If worldwide taxable turnover from online software/digital services exceeds CHF 100,000 p.a., apply for Swiss VAT identification (MWST-Registrierung) with the ESTV; register for employee withholding tax (Quellensteuer) once staff are employed; request the UID business identifier.
required_dossiers: Commercial register certificate of registration
Completed registration questionnaires (cantonal and federal)
Statutory seat, management structure and UBO information
Projected turnover declaration for threshold assessment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Late VAT registration penalty can be mitigated by voluntary-disclosure proceedings (Selbstanzeige); any administrative decision of the ESTV is contestable within 30 days by written objection (Einsprache) with subsequent appeal to the Federal Administrative Court.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: AHV, OASI, accident insurance, and workplace compliance registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Compensation Fund / AHV Administrative Body (AHV-Ausgleichskasse), Swiss National Accident Insurance Fund (SUVA) or licensed accident insurer, and the Cantonal Labour Inspectorate
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register as employer with the competent AHV compensation fund within the mandatory period, register a workers' accident insurance (UVG) contract with the company's chosen insurer and join the occupational health and safety service; file the annual sickness-day compensation declaration. Verify compliance of the office premises with VKF fire-safety approvals, structural occupancy-load requirements and the Labour Act (Arbeitsgesetz, SR 822.11) including ergonomic VDU workstations and staff safety briefing.
required_dossiers: Employer registration form with AHV-Ausgleichskasse
Commercial register certificate and board mandate
Insurance declarations (accident, sickness, loss-of-earnings replacement)
Fire safety and structural inspection certificates for the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the compensation fund demands an SIC/UVG declaration or a payroll record, submit the missing payroll documentation and the appointed insurer's confirmation retroactively; non-registration is regularised by a late-registration statement together with payment of arrears and tolerances available for first-time employers.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: No industrial licensing board applies to ISIC 5820 (software publishing) in Switzerland because the activity is non-manufacturing and non-physical; if premises are leased, only the cantonal building-authorisation authority and the Cantonal Economic Development Department (Wirtschaftskommission / Gewerbepolizei) may require a simple activity-announcement registration. The Federal Casino and Gambling Board (ESBK/Comlot, Eidgenössische Geldspielkommission) does not require a money-games licence for social casino/slot simulations without real-money stakes, given the Art. 3 (paras. 1a and 1b) BGS exclusion of gratuitous entertainments.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Exempt from a sectoral gaming licence; a mere Cantonal business-activity notification (Gewerbeanmeldung / annonce d'exploitation) to the commune of the registered office is sufficient where a physical front office is maintained.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Federal Office for the Environment (BAFU / OFEV / UFAM), together with the Cantonal Environment Protection Agency
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Full EIA Report not required and no Environmental Impact Assessment registration is triggered for software publishing and data-services operations under SR 814.011 (UVPV/EIA Ordinance); the project is classified as an office-based, low-impact activity, subject only to general environmental due-diligence duties under the Federal Environmental Protection Act (SR 814.01).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with the Air Pollution Control Ordinance (LRV, SR 814.318.142.1) Annex 2/4 VOC and particulate thresholds for any backup generators or office HVAC; Water Protection Ordinance (SR 814.201) discharge limits for sanitary wastewater and cooling water; Technical Waste Ordinance (SR 814.600) for segregated e-waste and lithium-battery recycling of server-discontinued hardware; facility must avoid ozone-depleting emissions and confirm absence of heavy-metal exhaust loads from digital activity.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Cantonal fire-certification certificate (VKF/AEAI Gebrauchs- und Funktionsabnahme) for the leasehold office, structural load-inspection certificate per SIA 261 for the selected premises, occupational workplace clearance under the Federal Labour Act (SR 822.11) covering VDU ergonomics, emergency exits and first-aid equipment, and employer enrolment in the SUVA accident clearance and safety-co-operation programme; data centres used for the digital game platform must be operated by a certified Swiss TIER-III provider with verifiable business-continuity clearance.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (Eidgenoessische Steuerverwaltung, ESTV / Administration federale des contributions, AFC) - VAT Main Division, Berne; official portals: www.estv.admin.ch for guidance and filings, 'Fiscus' as the secure e-communication and VAT return filing platform, www.zefix.ch for the central commercial register, and www.uid.admin.ch for the Unified Business Identifier (UID) register.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1 - Incorporate the Aktiengesellschaft (AG) in the cantonal commercial register (Zefix); the company automatically receives the UID (Unternehmens-Identifikationsnummer), which is the base Swiss tax identification number for all tax relations. Step 2 - Apply for Swiss VAT registration with the FTA/ESTV if annual taxable turnover exceeds CHF 100,000 (resident taxpayer, Art. 10 para. 1 and 2 MWSTG) or if the company is a non-resident supplier of electronic services to Swiss private consumers (mandatory from the first franc, Art. 10 para. 3 MWSTG); the FTA issues the MWST-Nr (VAT number, UID-based) normally within 2-4 weeks on Form 201/202 registration. Step 3 - Non-resident digital publisher without Swiss seat: use the simplified registration procedure (vereinfachte Steueranmeldung) under Art. 67-69 MWSTG, appoint a Swiss tax representative (domiciliary agent) and obtain a Swiss VAT ID even in the absence of a permanent establishment. Step 4 - Cantonal direct tax registration: only if a Swiss permanent establishment, office or employees exist, register the AG for corporate income tax and net wealth tax with the competent cantonal tax administration (e.g., Zug); a pure offshore/foreign-routed app-publishing activity with no Swiss substance does not trigger cantonal registration. Step 5 - Gaming-specific clearance: obtain a legal memorandum confirming that pure simulated social casino (no real-money payout, no withdrawal) is not a game of chance under the Swiss Federal Gambling Act (Geldspielgesetz) and therefore requires no gambling concession; licensed real-money online casinos are VAT-exempt under Art. 21 para. 2 no. 16 MWSTG, while unlicensed social casino IAP remains standard-rated at 8.1%.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation - The Swiss AG is a fully taxable separate legal person, subject to Swiss corporate income tax at federal, cantonal and communal level (federal statutory rate 8.5% after tax, approximately 18% effective before cantonal/communal relief; Zug combined effective rate around 11.9%) and to cantonal net wealth tax on equity. Unlimited tax liability applies for worldwide income with territorial carve-outs for foreign permanent establishments and foreign real estate (exemption with progression). Switzerland does not recognize check-the-box or any pass-through election for an AG. For Swiss VAT, the AG is a taxable person under Art. 10 MWSTG with full input VAT deduction rights on costs attributable to taxable and zero-rated export supplies; mixed-use input VAT is apportioned under Art. 30-31 MWSTG.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box election exists; classification follows Swiss corporate law. Available elections and statutory mechanisms: (i) VAT group taxation (Gruppenbesteuerung, Art. 21 para. 3 MWSTG) consolidating Swiss-resident group companies into one VAT person; (ii) participation relief election on qualified dividends and capital gains (Beteiligungsabzug, Art. 69 DBG) subject to minimum 10% shareholding or CHF 1,000,000 participation value; (iii) notional interest deduction (NID) on qualifying excess Swiss equity (Art. 25a-25b DBG, in force since 2020), particularly used by Zug financing/treasury entities; (iv) election of the small-business VAT exemption (Art. 11 MWSTG) for residents under CHF 100,000 turnover, not available to non-resident digital suppliers; (v) no hybrid-mismatch election - Swiss law statutorily denies deductions for hybrid financial instruments, hybrid entities and reverse hybrids under Art. 8a DBG and Art. 61a VStG (BEPS Action 2 alignment), so financing and royalty structures must be documented as non-abusive.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Swiss Value Added Tax (Mehrwertsteuer / Taxe sur la valeur ajoutee), governed by the Federal Act on Value Added Tax of 12 June 2009 (MWSTG), administered by the ESTV.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CHF 100,000 annual worldwide taxable turnover for Swiss-resident businesses and for non-resident B2B service suppliers where the Swiss recipient is liable for tax (Art. 10 para. 1 and 2 MWSTG); ZERO threshold for non-resident suppliers of electronic services (including downloadable social casino apps and in-app purchases) to private consumers resident in Switzerland - registration is mandatory from the first transaction (Art. 10 para. 3 MWSTG). Reduced rates: 2.6% (basic necessities) and 3.8% (accommodation); digital gaming/IAP supplies always attract the 8.1% standard rate.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Switzerland has NO real-time fiscal clearance, no continuous transaction controls, no API tax-stamping and no mandatory state e-invoicing comparable to Latin American or EU models. VAT reporting is period-based: taxpayers file periodic returns (quarterly, half-yearly or annually) electronically to the ESTV via the secure Fiscus portal. Invoices must contain the mandatory elements of Art. 26 MWSTG (name and address of supplier, VAT ID, recipient, date, type and quantity of supply, consideration, and VAT amount/rate). Since 1 July 2020, all payments referencing a Swiss QR-IBAN must use the standardized Swiss QR-bill (QR-Rechnung) with embedded QR code; this is a payment-slip standard, not a tax clearance stamp. All e-invoices and underlying accounting vouchers must be retained in an electronically verifiable format for 10 years (Art. 958f of the Swiss Code of Obligations) and must be made available to ESTV auditors in a structured data export upon request.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under Art. 23 para. 1 no. 1 and Art. 37 MWSTG, exported goods and exported services are exempt with input VAT deduction (effective 0% rate). For a Swiss AG publishing simulated social casino via Apple IAP and Google Play Billing: (i) B2B supply of game licences, sublicences or advertising services to foreign app-store operators or foreign advertisers: place of receipt abroad, 0% with full input VAT recovery; (ii) B2C in-app purchases by foreign consumers: place of supply is the consumer's residence (Art. 18 para. 1 letter d MWSTG), therefore outside Switzerland, 0%; (iii) B2C supplies to Swiss consumers: Swiss place of supply, standard 8.1% (no reduced rate). To sustain 0%, the AG must demonstrate the residence of each foreign customer through app-store billing-address data, Google Play/Apple App Store country codes, payment-card issuer country, geolocation/IP evidence and platform settlement reports. Where Apple or Google acts as merchant of record, the platform usually discharges Swiss VAT on Swiss consumer sales; the AG must retain the platform invoices and settlement statements to avoid double assessment of the same IAP consideration. Simulated social casino without real-money payout is not licensed Swiss gambling, so the Art. 21 para. 2 no. 16 MWSTG exemption does not apply.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Ausfuhrbegleitschein/AEB) - mandatory only for physical dispatches incident to gaming hardware or promotional merchandise; for pure digital downloads this item is substituted by platform sales and subscriber reports
Bill of Lading / CMR / Airwaybill - transport evidence required when physical goods are exported; not applicable to downloadable app content, replaced by ISP and platform traffic evidence
Inward Remittance Certificate - bank and payment service provider (PSP) credit records evidencing net proceeds credited to the Swiss AG from foreign app-store operators and advertising counterparties

App-Store Sales and Subscriber Reports - Apple App Store Connect and Google Play Console monthly country-level billing files (ISO 3166 customer codes, bill-to addresses, payment-country data, purchase timestamps)
Merchant-of-Record Platform Invoices - Apple/Google consolidated VAT invoices and settlement statements showing the foreign platform as reseller or disclosed agent for Swiss consumer sales
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The ESTV's VAT division specifically targets zero-rated digital exporters (MWST-Info 02, electronic services) and applies higher risk scoring to social/gaming apps because of in-app purchase complexity and platform commission flows. If the 0% export rate is claimed without contemporaneous residence evidence, the FTA retrospectively recharacterizes the supply as Swiss-taxable: output VAT is assessed on the full consideration, input VAT is clawed back, and default interest accrues under Art. 87 MWSTG from the statutory due date. Retrospective reassessment is statute-barred after 5 years for ordinary errors but extends to 10 years where tax evasion is shown (Art. 39 para. 2 MWSTG). Penalties: breach of procedural duties - warning up to CHF 10,000 (Art. 70 MWSTG); negligent understatement - fine up to one-third of the evaded tax (Art. 71 para. 2 MWSTG); intentional evasion, including fabricated export documentation, sham merchant-of-record arrangements or shell-company routing of app proceeds - fine up to 4 times the evaded tax (Art. 71 para. 1 MWSTG), plus criminal prosecution under Articles 186-187 of the Swiss Penal Code for fraudulent tax evasion (imprisonment up to 3 years, up to 10 years for organized constellations); directors and compliance officers are individually liable. Switzerland imposes no statutory FX repatriation deadline; the 180-day figure in this dossier is applied as an internal treasury benchmark for verified FX conversion and documentary completeness of export consideration.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Swiss National Bank (SNB) / Schweizerische Nationalbank / Banque nationale suisse / Banca nazionale svizzera; responsible for monetary policy, currency issuance and financial system stability; no comprehensive foreign-exchange-control mandate; FINMA supervises banking and money-laundering conduct.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Swiss franc is fully convertible on both current and capital account. Swiss law does not distinguish between residents and non-residents for foreign-exchange purposes and imposes no exchange-control approval on dividends, profit remittances, loan repayments, royalties or licence fees. The only material hurdles are corporate and tax formalities, including the Swiss 35% anticipatory withholding tax on certain profit distributions and treaty-based relief or refund procedures. Cross-border revenues from social-casino app sales are treated as ordinary service or goods receipts and may be converted or remitted freely.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Switzerland has no statutory surrender obligation, no mandatory conversion ratio and no fixed timeline for export receipts. An exporter may retain, invest or convert proceeds in any currency; only anti-money-laundering reporting thresholds, tax return disclosure and, where applicable, statistical surveys of the Swiss National Bank apply.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low for offshore digital EMIs as a primary treasury rail; Medium for FINMA-licensed or fintech-supervised payment institutions as ancillary transaction sub-accounts. An offshore EMI cannot passport an EU or UK licence into Switzerland and cannot access SIC or offer Swiss-located CHF account numbers without a Swiss banking partner or FINMA licence. Use such EMIs only for ancillary multicurrency collection; keep the main escrow and operating liquidity in a Swiss-licensed bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is not a universal statutory mandate. FINMA-compliant remote video identification is accepted by many Swiss banks for natural-person controllers, and account opening may be effected by a duly authorised representative. However, for gaming-adjacent sectors and non-resident beneficial owners, banks ordinarily require board-level interviews and documentary confirmation of the controllers. Expect at least one in-person or video interview with the substance of the directors and a notarised extract from the Swiss Commercial Register; remote-only onboarding may be refused at the bank's discretion.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Gambling-adjacent business model: 'social casino', virtual slots and in-app coin purchases may be classified as disguised online gambling by a Swiss AML officer.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A formal Swiss legal opinion under the Geldspielgesetz / Gesetz über Geldspiele classifying the product as non-gambling because coins have no real-money value, no cash prizes, no convertibility to real-world reward and no secondary market; certified game design documents; RNG and self-exclusion controls; App Store and Google Play policy attestations; jurisdiction-specific availability restrictions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk foreign beneficial ownership or opaque source-of-wealth for non-resident founders.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full corporate ownership chain to natural persons; Swiss Commercial Register extract; notarised articles of association; valid passport copies; bank and professional references; source-of-wealth and source-of-funds statement supported by bank statements, sale agreements, tax returns or audited financial statements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border app-store disbursement and high-volume micro-transaction flows create unusual inbound receipts, potential third-party payment mixing and chargeback concentration.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed Apple Developer Program and Google Play agreements; merchant payout bank statements; reconciliation files such as Apple Financial Report and Google Play financial reports; treasury policy against aggregated third-party settlement; chargeback policy; KYC screening of enterprise users; segregation of player funds if any.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Potential Swiss tax leakage or undeclared revenues from Swiss players and VAT or excise exposure.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Swiss tax counsel comfort letter on income and VAT treatment; registration status with the Swiss Federal Tax Administration and relevant canton; intercompany profit documentation; transfer-pricing file, including royalty and licensing calculations for intellectual property held in Switzerland or abroad.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of virtual tokens, software or player balances creating DLT or security classification, or unlicensed deposit-taking concerns.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: FINMA DLT and blockchain guidance assessment confirming no securities or payment-system licence threshold; technical token versus account-balance documentation; independent IT and legal opinion on non-transferability and absence of deposit-like features; AML/CFT policy and suspicious-transaction reporting procedures.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: For the initial CHF 100,000 Aktiengesellschaft share capital and any subsequent capital increase, route via SWIFT MT103 for single payments or MT202/MT203 for higher-value transactions to the target Swiss account; in the instruction or reference field use 'Einlage / Dotierung / Kapitalerhöhung' and identify the legal entity. Switzerland imposes no purpose-code or FX-approval requirement, but the bank will verify the corporate resolution, notarial deed and Swiss Commercial Register filing, and will issue an Einlagebestätigung or equity confirmation. Foreign-currency subscriptions may be converted at the bank's spot rate without surrender restrictions.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use SWIFT MT103 for cross-border trade settlements, supplier invoices, royalties and group payments; MT202 or MT203 for interbank liquidity and treasury concentration; SIC or Swiss Instant Payments for CHF domestic flows; SEPA Credit Transfer or TARGET2 for EUR; and Fedwire or CHIPS for USD. A Commercial Letter of Credit is acceptable for physical goods or equipment procurement but is not the standard rail for software or Apple and Google IAP settlements. IAP proceeds should be received directly from Apple or Google payout systems into a designated operational account; reconcile store payout files against MT940 or MT950 account statements on a daily or weekly cycle.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain-vanilla FX forwards (deliverable) under ISDA/Credit Support Annex or bank-format master agreement
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for restricted or illiquid emerging-market currencies not traded against CHF
Cross-currency swaps and currency swaps for long-term balance-sheet hedging
FX options, including purchased options and zero-premium collars, subject to bank credit and board-approved risk limits

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Meeting - approval of annual financial statements, allocation of profit, discharge of the Board of Directors and auditors
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: No government filing; AGM minutes and attendance records retained at registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months of the 31 December balance-sheet date (by 30 June); convening notice at least 20 days before the meeting (Art. 699-700 CO)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No direct monetary penalty; failure to organize may trigger shareholders' annulment actions, director liability under Art. 754 CO, and court-ordered dissolution of the AG

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Deposit of the annual financial statements and statutory audit report at the Commercial Register (mandatory for ordinary-audit companies, Art. 958e CO)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt) and Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (SHAB/SOGC) publication
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 12 months of the balance-sheet date; immediately after approval by the AGM (practically by the following 31 December for a 31.12 FYE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Registrar imposes an enforcement deadline and disciplinary fine up to CHF 5,000 (Art. 943 CO); continued default may lead to bankruptcy declaration and ex officio deregistration

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Cantonal and federal corporate income tax return (annual Steuererklärung) including capital tax declaration for the AG
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal tax administration (e.g., Steuerverwaltung Zug) acting for both cantonal and Direct Federal Tax (DBG), Federal Tax Administration (ESTV)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filed by 31 March of the year following the calendar tax year; extension to 30 September, or 31 December where accounts are prepared by a licensed Swiss fiduciary
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default interest of 4.5% p.a.; late-filing and negligence penalties; tax-evasion fine up to 100% of the evaded tax, up to 300% in aggravated cases (Art. 175-176 DBG); criminal referral

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Swiss VAT return - fourth quarter settlement and annual VAT status (standard rate 8.1% applies to social-casino virtual goods sold to Swiss end consumers via Apple/Google in-app purchase)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Quarterly return within 60 days after quarter-end; annual filing option for turnover below CHF 5,005,000 (return due within 60 days after 31 December)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default interest of 4.5% p.a.; penal surcharge up to 100% of VAT withheld or concealed (Art. 91 Swiss VAT Act); criminal prosecution for VAT fraud

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Withholding tax return and payment (35% Verrechnungssteuer) on dividends or other profit distributions resolved by the AGM
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Federal Tax Administration (ESTV), withholding tax division
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after the AGM resolution declaring the distribution (Art. 12-12bis VStG)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default interest of 3% p.a.; penalty up to 100% of the withholding tax evaded; personal enforcement against responsible directors

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual verification of the Register of Beneficial Owners (UBO register), notification of >25% shareholding transfers, and filing of the 'no beneficial owner' declaration where applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Register kept at registered office; 'no UBO' declaration delivered to the Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Art. 697l para 2 CO)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Board re-verification no later than the AGM (by 30 June); UBO register entries updated within 30 days after any indirect or direct stake reaches or exceeds 25% (Art. 697m CO)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines up to CHF 10,000 per violation for breach of UBO record-keeping and notification duties (Art. 697o CO); criminal exposure under Art. 305bis Swiss Criminal Code for omission of control information

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Ordinary (full) audit is mandatory if the AG exceeds any two of the three size tests in two consecutive financial years: balance sheet total above CHF 20 million, annual turnover above CHF 40 million, or annual average of more than 250 full-time employees; ordinary audit is also required for listed issuers, bond issuers, and licensed regulated financial institutions (Art. 727 CO). All other AGs must undergo a limited audit (eingeschränkte Revision) unless the company has fewer than 10 full-time employees on annual average and all shareholders validly resolve to dispense with the audit (Art. 727a CO)
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Swiss Code of Obligations accounting law (Art. 957-962b CO) serving as Swiss GAAP; Swiss GAAP FER is the national standard for medium-size and group reporting; IFRS may be applied alternatively (Art. 962a CO); financial statements are drawn in CHF and the authoritative principle (Massgeblichkeitsprinzip) binds tax accounts to the statutory balance sheet and income statement

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: On an annual basis the Board must confirm and date-sign the internal Register of Beneficial Owners (Art. 697j-697k CO) listing every natural person who directly or indirectly holds more than 25% of shares or voting rights or controls the AG. A shareholder crossing the 25% threshold must notify the Board within 30 days; the Board updates the register within 30 days and follows the same rule for any transfer that terminates significant ownership. The register is not publicly filed but must be made available to the Commercial Register and prosecutorial authorities on request; absent a qualifying UBO, a written declaration to that effect must be delivered to the Commercial Register Office each time it becomes inaccurate. For the federal transparency register (LTEO) once operational, the AG must submit the initial UBO dataset to the Federal Register of Beneficial Owners within the first reporting cycle and thereafter confirm annual changes via the federal e-portal
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Aktienbuch) recording registered-share ownership, bearer-share issuance, and transfers
Register of Directors with specimen signatures and board delegation minutes
Minute Book containing AGM and board minutes and all resolutions
Register of Beneficial Owners (wirtschaftlich Berechtigte / ayants droit économiques) under Art. 697j-697m CO

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,100-3,800 per year (approx. CHF 1,000-3,500) for a licensed Swiss registered-office and corporate-administration agency in Zug or Geneva, excluding fiduciary accounting services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 4,500-42,000 per year depending on engagement: limited audit/review CHF 4,000-12,000; full ordinary statutory audit CHF 10,000-38,000; optional audit dispensation reduces cost to the statutory reviewer's written confirmation fee; add-ons apply for multi-jurisdictional Apple IAP and Google Play Billing revenue-trace verification for social-casino releases

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 18.0% (combined federal, cantonal, and communal effective rate; federal rate 8.5% plus cantonal/communal)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Patent box regime (reduced taxation of qualifying IP income), notional interest deduction (NID) on excess equity, R&D super deduction (150% of qualifying R&D costs), and participation exemption for substantial shareholdings.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Federal and cantonal corporate tax return (Formula for legal entities / Steuererklärung juristische Personen) filed electronically via the Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV) ePortal or cantonal tax office e-filing system (e.g., SwissTax, eTax).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 6 months after fiscal year-end, extendable upon written request to the competent tax authority.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company identification (name, registered address, UID number)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident companies with a Swiss permanent establishment (PE) must identify the PE and its Swiss address.
State the PE's fiscal year, which must align with the parent company's fiscal year unless otherwise approved.
Report only Swiss-source income attributable to the PE; apply arm's length principle for internal transactions.
For PE, allocate capital based on the PE's actual economic substance and asset allocation.
Claim participation exemption for qualifying dividends and capital gains; provide supporting documentation.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalties up to CHF 5,000 plus daily surcharges of 0.5% of the assessed tax (max 10%); additional fines for willful non-compliance.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 35% (reduced to 0% under participation exemption if holding ≥10% for at least 1 year)
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke DTA relief, submit Form 823 (for dividends) or equivalent to the Swiss Federal Tax Administration, accompanied by a valid Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from the recipient's country of residence. Reduced rates apply as per the applicable DTA; refunds are processed within 3-6 months.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: 0% (no Swiss WHT on royalties). Interest: 0% (no Swiss WHT on interest). However, anti-abuse rules (e.g., substance requirements) may apply to deny treaty benefits.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File required if turnover > CHF 50 million; Master File required if group turnover > CHF 1 billion.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Switzerland does not have a specific Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) regime, but requires real economic substance (office, staff, decision-making) to establish tax residency and to benefit from DTAs. Anti-abuse rules (e.g., GAAR) apply to shell companies.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willful misrepresentation or concealment of income, assets, or transactions to reduce tax liability (e.g., underreporting revenue from virtual slots).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal fines up to CHF 250,000 and imprisonment up to 3 years; additional civil penalties of up to 3 times the evaded tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be held personally liable for restitution of evaded taxes, subject to travel bans and potential imprisonment if found complicit.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating as a letterbox company without real economic activity, staff, or premises in Switzerland, while claiming treaty benefits or tax incentives.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty benefits, retroactive tax assessments, and penalties up to CHF 100,000; potential reclassification as a transparent entity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally liable for unpaid taxes and penalties if they knowingly facilitated the sham structure; travel bans may be imposed.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to implement adequate anti-money laundering (AML) controls for in-app purchases and virtual currency transactions, or knowingly processing proceeds from illegal gambling.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines up to CHF 500,000 and imprisonment up to 5 years for individuals; corporate fines up to CHF 5 million; revocation of business licenses.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors face personal criminal liability, including imprisonment, and may be subject to asset freezes and travel bans.
